title: Weighted Cauchy–Riemann estimates and holomorphic peaks
source_hypothesis: Any open planar domain and real C2 strictly subharmonic weight. Weighted square-integrable forcing with inverse-Laplacian density. Peak size and all derivative estimates are uniform on a prescribed relatively compact open set containing the interpolation point; the constructed function is holomorphic on the full original domain.
reviewed_arguments: The weighted equation is posed on an arbitrary open subset of the plane with a real C2 weight and strictly positive Laplacian. No boundary regularity or global curvature minimum is assumed.
The exact adjoint convention and commutator give the curvature term Delta Phi / 4. Compact supports remove every boundary term.

A bounded antilinear functional on the actual weighted derivative range yields a solution by the proved Hilbert projection and representation theorem. The solution is orthogonal to the nullspace and has minimal norm.
The passage back to ordinary distributional tests explicitly approximates e^Phi times a smooth test in C1; it does not silently upgrade the weight from C2 to smooth.
Circle means follow from the Cauchy–Riemann equation and periodic integration. Radial averaging proves every local derivative estimate and weak holomorphic regularity by mollification.
The localized fundamental kernel includes the exact factor 1/pi. The pointwise estimate retains the nonzero forcing term, including at points in the cutoff annulus.
The holomorphic quadratic polynomial has the exact Taylor coefficient phi_zz and gap Delta phi / 4. The annular forcing is smooth across the interpolation point.

The rescaled weight 2 log(t) phi gives the actual correction on the original domain with squared weighted norm bounded by C t^(-2 epsilon) / log(t). Only the forcing support needs a positive curvature minimum.
The radius 1/log(t) keeps the local weight ratio bounded. The forced pointwise estimate controls the correction uniformly on a fixed larger compact set.
The correction vanishes at the interpolation point and cancels its Cauchy–Riemann derivative exactly. Every real derivative obeys the logarithmic bound on one fixed open set.
The Gaussian exercise proves the constant four is sharp using orthogonality to the holomorphic nullspace; the exact quadratic peak distinguishes normalized modulus from a holomorphic maximum.

This supplies the two weighted/peaking analytic tools in H4 26.2.5–26.2.6. It does not claim the subsequent complex-leaf propagation or prescribed-regularity theorem, nor completion of H4 26.2–26.11 or the whole course.
